case_title: State of A.P. v. M. Sohan Babu & Anr.
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PWs 1-4 and neighbour-linked testimony), medical evidence
aggravating_circumstances: Entry at midnight armed with knives for robbery; knives used repeatedly and effectively; neighbours also injured and threatened with dire consequences
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.302/34, 460 and 324; sentence terms not stated in the judgment
high_court_outcome: Conviction under s.302 altered to s.304 Part I; acquitted of s.302
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 r/w s.34 (trial court conviction restored); s.460 and s.324 convictions as per trial court judgment
neutral_facts: During the intervening night of 20th/21st November 1991, shortly after midnight, the victim heard footsteps in a shared two-floor residential building and came out to investigate. He found one accused standing on the first-floor balcony. A scuffle followed, and shouts drew other occupants, who saw the victim and that accused grappling. The victim pinned the accused to the ground. The accused then drew a knife and stabbed the victim in the left side of the abdomen. A second accused, who had come from the balcony side, stabbed the victim on both thighs. When a relative tried to help, the first accused stabbed him in the right arm. The second accused held a knife at the throat of another relative and stabbed a further relative in the left shoulder. Other occupants and neighbours arrived, overpowered the accused, and tied them up on the ground floor. Police were informed. The victim was taken to a railway hospital but died on the way. Other injured persons received first aid, and their injuries were found to be simple. The evidence consisted of eyewitness testimony from several family members and a neighbour, supported by medical evidence.
physical_harm: Victim died from stab injuries to abdomen and thighs; a relative stabbed in the right arm and another in the left shoulder; other injured had simple injuries
number_of_offences: 3 charged; 3 finally upheld (trial court judgment restored)
premeditation_planning: No finding of premeditation to cause death; court noted entry armed with intent to rob
motive: Robbery (initial purpose accepted by the court)
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness account that A2 stabbed the victim in the abdomen while pinned; further thigh injuries by both accused; injuries to neighbours and threats
witness_credibility: Not separately assessed; court accepted the in-evidence account of the injuries and threats and rejected the High Court's reading of the evidence
post_offence_conduct: Both accused were overpowered and tied up by occupants; police informed; no other post-offence conduct noted
trial_duration: offence: 20th/21st November 1991; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 11.12.2003; Supreme Court: December 14, 2010
legal_representation: Appellant (State): I. Venkatanarayana, Ramesh Allanki, D. Mahesh Babu; Respondents (accused): Anil Kumar Tandale, Manoj C. Mishra, Brajesh Jha
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.302/34, 460, 324. High Court: s.302 conviction altered to s.304 Part I. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, High Court part set aside, trial court judgment restored
prosecution_argument: State challenged High Court's alteration of the s.302 conviction; no detailed arguments recorded in the judgment
legal_principle_applied: Common intention under s.34 may be inferred from circumstances arising during the incident; intention to cause death assessed from the conduct and weapons used
judicial_aggravating_factors: Knives used repeatedly and effectively; willingness to kill; entry armed at midnight; injuries and threats to neighbours
